title: New-Customer Protection Multiplier for Off-Peak Billing Disputes (Residential Electricity Supply)
content:
**Rule.** On a Residential Electricity Supply off-peak billing dispute, when the agreement's enrollment date is 365 or fewer calendar days before the referral date, the over-billed amount is multiplied by the first-year protection factor of 1.1; when it is 366 to 730 calendar days before, by the second-year protection factor of 1.05; when it is more than 730 calendar days before, the over-billed amount is taken as it stands.

**Dates read.** The enrollment date is the date the customer authorized the enrollment, as recorded on the agreement; it is not the service start date. The referral date is the date the dispute is referred to billing review. The days are the referral date less the enrollment date, in calendar days.

| Calendar days from enrollment date to referral date | Over-billed amount is |
|---|---|
| 365 or fewer | multiplied by 1.1 |
| 366 to 730 | multiplied by 1.05 |
| more than 730 | taken as it stands |

**Boundaries (hypothetical enrollment date 2024-03-01).** A referral on 2025-03-01 is 365 days later and takes 1.1; on 2025-03-02 it is 366 days and takes 1.05; on 2026-03-01 it is 730 days and takes 1.05; on 2026-03-02 it is 731 days and is taken as it stands.

**Example (hypothetical).** An over-billed amount of 160.00 USD on an agreement enrolled 200 days before the referral becomes 176.00 USD.
